source.title: Mice adaptively generate choice variability in a deterministic task

confidence_rationale: Directly and rigorously supports the source thought's 'variability must not automatically be classified as noise' section: mice in a task with a fully deterministic reward structure nonetheless actively generated increasing choice variability, converging on a randomness LEVEL that maximized reward under uncertainty about the true rule, rather than following a fixed-sequence strategy that a naive optimality analysis would predict. The study additionally provides a worked example of GOV-BEHADJ-1's 'Perturb' step done well: a discriminating behavioral-switch test distinguishes the randomness-strategy explanation from a memorized-sequence explanation. High confidence given the rigor of the design, though mapping fidelity to REE's richer spatial/naturalistic Fishtank environment is only moderate.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a task with deterministic, fixed reward rules that in principle permitted a 100%-success fixed sequence, mice instead progressively increased the variability (Lempel-Ziv complexity) of their choice sequences across sessions, converging on ~75% success matching a near-random selection strategy rather than continuing to seek the deterministic 100% solution. A follow-up behavioral-switch test -- introducing probabilistic (75%) rewards after training on the deterministic task -- found mice did NOT change their behavior, indicating they had learned a general randomness-generation STRATEGY rather than a specific rewarded sequence, and first-order/second-order Markov analysis of their choice sequences showed no exploitable patterned structure remained, i.e. the variability was not merely inconsistent performance but an actively regulated, close-to-optimal randomization strategy.
mapping.ree_translation: This is close to a worked demonstration of the source thought's own methodological aspiration, in a different organism and task. The source thought asks: 'did randomness become differently organised?' rather than merely 'did behaviour become less random?' -- Belkaid et al. answer a structurally identical question for real animals with a rigorous discriminating design: a reward-structure manipulation (deterministic task) that should, on the naive optimal-sequence account, eliminate variability, paired with a switch-test perturbation that discriminates 'learned a specific sequence' (would predict behavior change under the switch) from 'learned a randomness strategy' (predicts no change, as observed). If GOV-BEHADJ-1's proposed workflow is hardened into a REE skill, this paper is a directly citable template for how to test whether REE's own stochastic exploratory behavior is adaptively regulated (a policy-level randomness parameter tuned to task uncertainty) versus passive noise, using an analogous discriminating perturbation rather than a global entropy/tortuosity metric alone.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The task is a simplified binary/discrete operant choice paradigm (a small decision tree with few branches), not a rich, continuous spatial navigation environment like Fishtank -- the specific complexity metric used (Lempel-Ziv complexity of a short choice sequence) would need substantial adaptation for a spatial trajectory domain with a much larger state space. The deterministic-reward manipulation is also a much cleaner, more controlled environment than Fishtank's naturalistic multi-feature (refuge/food/hazard) layout.
mapping.source_context: Head-fixed or freely-moving mice performing a binary choice task with a decision-tree reward structure; deterministic-reward and probabilistic-reward (behavioral switch test) conditions; computational modeling of a randomness-parameter-tuning decision process; first- and second-order Markov analysis of resulting choice sequences.

confidence_components.notes: Rigorous, peer-reviewed study combining behavioral, computational-modeling, and discriminating-perturbation methods in a single design, published in a reputable Nature-family journal. Mapping fidelity moderate-high: the underlying logic (test whether variability is adaptively regulated via a discriminating perturbation, not just measured with a global statistic) transfers well even though the specific task and complexity metric would need REE-specific reimplementation.
